title: Well-balanced balance laws and wet/dry fronts

items.title: One-dimensional shallow-water balance law with a dry-state convention
items.statement: For g>0 and a stationary bed b(x), define U=(h,m), the admissible wet/dry state set, velocity, physical flux including its dry value, the balance-law source, and lake-at-rest profiles.
items.strategy: Fix conserved-variable, dry-state, flux, source, free-surface and equilibrium conventions explicitly.

items.title: Hydrostatic reconstruction with a dry-safe HLL flux and one-sided pressure corrections
items.statement: Define the max-bed hydrostatic states, dry-safe HLL flux branches and speeds, left/right corrected fluxes, finite-volume update, source decomposition and face-specific CFL.
items.strategy: State every input, branch including the all-dry case, corrected flux orientation, update and cellwise CFL.

items.title: A strong local L1 limit preserves shallow-water dry admissibility
items.statement: A strong local L1 limit of nonnegative depths remains nonnegative; with m=hu and u=0 on dry points, the limit state lies in K.
items.strategy: Bound the negative part of the limit by the L1 error on a countable compact exhaustion, then use the dry velocity convention.

items.title: The shallow-water wet/dry state set is convex
items.statement: The set K={(h,m):h>0,m in R} union {(0,0)} is convex, so it is an admissible convex state set in the PE03 sense.
items.strategy: Check a convex combination by its nonnegative depth; zero depth forces both input depths and momenta to vanish.

items.title: HLL depth flux is a bounded outflow/inflow combination
items.statement: At each face write the HLL mass flux as p h_L^* - q h_R^* with 0<=p<=a_R and 0<=q<=-a_L, including equality-speed branches; the coefficient multiplying a positive reconstructed side is strictly below its outgoing wave-speed bound.
items.strategy: Expand the middle HLL formula and check the two equality-speed branches separately.

items.title: A dry HLL face sends water only into the dry side
items.statement: If the reconstructed right state is dry, the HLL depth flux is nonnegative; if the reconstructed left state is dry, it is nonpositive; in either case a zero depth flux implies the full HLL vector flux is zero.
items.strategy: Check the zero-speed and middle branches; positive wet depth makes the corresponding HLL mass coefficient strictly positive.

items.title: The hydrostatic HLL update preserves lakes at rest, including dry cells
items.statement: For any discrete bed, a rest profile with common free-surface level on wet cells and dry cells above that level has zero update under the hydrostatic corrected fluxes.
items.strategy: Show the reconstructed states agree at each face, evaluate the consistent HLL flux, and cancel the one-sided corrected cell pressures.

items.title: The hydrostatic HLL step conserves water and preserves nonnegative depth
items.statement: Under lambda(a_R at the right face - a_L at the left face)<=1 in every cell, one update preserves K, hence h>=0 and m=0 at h=0; shared mass fluxes conserve total water on a periodic mesh and change finite-domain water only by boundary discharge.
items.strategy: Expand the depth update into nonnegative inflows and bounded outflows, prove wet depths stay positive and dry cells cannot gain momentum at zero depth, then telescope the shared first-component flux.

items.title: Hydrostatic pressure corrections converge to the smooth-bed source
items.statement: For b in C^2 and bounded nonnegative cell depths, the scheme's source residual is -g h_i b'(x_i)+O(Delta x) uniformly on compact sets; strong local L1 convergence of reconstructed depths gives strong local L1 convergence to (0,-g h b').
items.strategy: Taylor-expand the adjacent bed increments, use the positive-part identity and a uniform quadratic remainder, then pass the depth factor through strong L1 convergence.

items.title: Exact space-time weak identity for the hydrostatic update
items.statement: Testing the source-decomposed vector update by space-time cell averages gives the exact discrete weak identity with the initial term, shared HLL face fluxes and discrete source.
items.strategy: Multiply the vector recurrence, telescope in time, reindex shared face fluxes in space, and retain the source term.

items.title: Hydrostatic HLL face fluxes converge under strong state and velocity convergence
items.statement: Under AC_omega, strong local L1 convergence of depths, velocities and conserved states, local uniform depth/velocity bounds, a Lipschitz bed and vanishing mesh width, the reconstructed HLL face flux converges strongly in L1loc to the physical shallow-water flux.
items.strategy: Use L1 translation continuity for neighboring cells, show hydrostatic height clipping is O(Delta x) and velocity resets vanish near dry limits, then use HLL diagonal continuity and a uniform flux bound.

items.title: A strong limit of hydrostatic HLL updates solves the smooth-bed balance law weakly
items.statement: Assume AC_omega, b in C^2, vanishing space/time steps, local uniform depth/velocity bounds, strong local L1 convergence of states and velocities to U=(h,hu), and local L1 convergence of the initial reconstructions. Then U satisfies the distributional shallow-water balance law with source (0,-g h b_x); convergence, source quadrature control and the initial trace are hypotheses, and no entropy or compactness conclusion follows.
items.strategy: Pass the exact vector discrete weak identity to the limit using the local face-flux and source-convergence lemmas, and retain the initial boundary term.

title: Well-balanced balance laws and wet/dry fronts — Examples

items.title: A lake at rest over a bump with a dry crest
items.statement: For g=1, bed values (0,1,2,1,0) and rest depths (2,1,0,1,2), all one-sided corrected fluxes match cell hydrostatic pressures and the update is zero.
items.strategy: Compute every shared reconstructed depth, HLL pressure flux, one-sided correction and cell-side cancellation.

items.title: A first HLL step wets a dry cell without negative depth
items.statement: For g=1, flat bed, one wet state (1,0) adjacent to dry states and lambda=1/2, the wet/dry HLL flux is (1/2,1/4), producing adjacent states (3/4,1/8) and (1/4,1/8).
items.strategy: Evaluate the all-dry, wet/wet and wet/dry face fluxes, check every local CFL and compute the two updated states exactly.

items.title: A centered pressure flux and centered bed source move a discrete lake
items.statement: The periodic three-cell lake with bed (0,1/2,0) and free-surface level 1 is stationary under every consistent centered pressure flux and centered source.
items.strategy: Specify one concrete central-flux/centered-source update and compute a nonzero momentum residual in one cell.
